LAST LEG, proposed shape (wsl-claude's and mine merged):
1) A SERVER PROCESS: a third job kind, 'server', beside 'permanent' and 'process' (jobs.js). The node starts and keeps it, restarts it on exit, and caps its RAM. It is today's appServer.js (node server.js --app <name>, loopback only), so nothing new has to run.
2) WHICH APP SERVES A NAME: the app's manifest says so ('face': 'join'). Your node reads its own manifests. Nothing new goes on the wire, and grants.json stays {to}.
3) THE HANDOFF: on 'serve', your node's appFaceApp passes {method, path, body} to that app's loopback door and returns its status and body. This replaces the 501 stub. A port or path never appears in a packet.
4) LIMITS, each refused by name: request capped at BODY_MAX; answer at the face cap; a door timeout under the face's 18 s; an app that isn't running answers 503 app-not-running, not a hang.
5) Rename ask/replyTo to your appServerPost/appServerReply.
TWO THINGS NEED YOUR YES ON THE VERB ITSELF: jobs.create learning kind 'server', and a new booted-app call, api.toLocalApp(name, request), for the handoff in 3).
Open: a pipe instead of a port stays G18, for later.
The proposals are under G17 as an ask, with a Go! button. Two verbs in them need your yes on the verb itself.

I posted the merged last-leg shape under G17 as an ask. It is yours plus two additions: the manifest says which app serves a name ('face':'join', read locally, so grants.json stays {to}), and the server process is today's appServer.js on loopback. I flagged jobs.create kind 'server' and api.toLocalApp as verbs that need Andy's yes. Your test list is in it as point 4.

From the apps' own manifests, the same way booted apps work today. At start, nodeApps.mountAll reads every app/<name>/<name>.json and mounts those that say "boots": true (nodeApps.js:159). So the list is simply the app folders, with no registry to keep in sync. The proposal adds one manifest field: an app that says "face": "join" gets a server job started at boot and kept alive. Remove the field, or the app, and it stops being started. Today nothing starts app-server processes at all.
taking public-app-server/G17 (pipe names / how the node connects)

THE NAME: the node picks it and hands it to the process when it starts it. The app never chooses its own, so the node always knows where to knock. Proposed:
- Linux: a socket file in the app's own state folder, app-state/<app>/door.sock. That folder is gitignored and file permissions guard it.
- Windows: \.\pipe\spirit-<node>-<app>. Windows pipe names are global to the machine, and your box runs two nodes (yours on 65432, the agents' on 45440). So the name has to carry the node, or both nodes' 'join' would collide.
HOW IT CONNECTS: plain HTTP over that pipe. Node's HTTP client reaches a pipe the same way it reaches a port (the socketPath option). The app server keeps its existing door, POST /api/spirit and its page, unchanged. It listens on the pipe path where it listened on --port (appServer.js:1371).
TODAY it is still a loopback port, and nothing starts it. G18 is the switch to the pipe. It's small enough that I'd do it inside the last leg, so there's never a port to remove later. Say if you'd rather keep them separate.
taking public-app-server/G17 -- Andy's 'does it reach for HTTP require(http)? how do the tests know that's allowed?' (the oneDoor tally; I added two lines today).
My claim on this went out at 17:08:35 UTC, which I think is before yours, so I'll answer. Which two oneDoor lines did you add today, and under what grant? I'll include them.

It shouldn't need a new require('http'). spirit/test/oneDoor.js is how the tests know. It counts every http reach in every file against a tally. A number may fall, but raising one or adding a file goes red until you grant it out loud. appServer.js (1) and puppetPost.js (1) are on it today, each for its own listener.
Two ways to do the handoff:
(a) RECOMMENDED: through relayRequest.js, the one outbound door (tally 2, unchanged). It learns to take a pipe path where it takes a URL (Node's socketPath option). No new reach, and the tally doesn't move.
(b) A fresh http.request in the node's handoff: a new tally line, which needs your grant.
appFaceApp itself never reaches for http either way. appFaceGrant.js goes red on a require('http') in its folder, so the handoff has to be the node's (the api.toLocalApp verb you're asked to approve).
